notes: The 6507 in the 2600 is a 6502 with 13 address lines (8 KB space, cartridge at $1000-$1FFF) and no IRQ/NMI pins.
CPU clock is the colour clock / 3: 76 CPU cycles per scanline (228 colour clocks).
Indexed reads (abs,X / abs,Y / (zp),Y) take +1 cycle when the effective address crosses a page; stores and read-modify-write always take it.
Branches: 2 cycles not taken, 3 taken, 4 taken to another page.
Zero-page indexed addressing wraps inside page 0 ($FF,X with X=2 reads $01).

ADC.description: A = A + M + C. In decimal mode (SED) the addition is BCD; on the NMOS 6502 N, V and Z are not valid after a decimal ADC.

ASL.description: Shifts left one bit; bit 7 goes to C, 0 enters bit 0.

BCC.description: Branches if C = 0. 2 cycles, +1 if taken, +1 more if the target is on another page.

BCS.description: Branches if C = 1. 2 cycles, +1 if taken, +1 more if the target is on another page.

BEQ.description: Branches if Z = 1. 2 cycles, +1 if taken, +1 more if the target is on another page.

BMI.description: Branches if N = 1. 2 cycles, +1 if taken, +1 more if the target is on another page.

BNE.description: Branches if Z = 0. 2 cycles, +1 if taken, +1 more if the target is on another page.

BPL.description: Branches if N = 0. 2 cycles, +1 if taken, +1 more if the target is on another page.

BVC.description: Branches if V = 0. 2 cycles, +1 if taken, +1 more if the target is on another page.

BVS.description: Branches if V = 1. 2 cycles, +1 if taken, +1 more if the target is on another page.

BIT.description: Z = (A & M) == 0; N and V take bits 7 and 6 of M. Common on the 2600 to test collision and input bits (D7/D6) without touching A. BIT abs is also used as a 'skip next 2 bytes' trick.

BRK.description: Pushes PC+2 and P (with B set) and jumps through $FFFE. The 6507 has no IRQ pin, so BRK is the only way to reach that vector.

CLD.description: D = 0. Power-on state of D is undefined: clear it at start-up.

CLI.description: I = 0. Irrelevant on the 6507 (no IRQ pin).

CMP.description: Computes A - M: C = A >= M, Z = A == M, N = bit 7 of the result.

CPX.description: Computes X - M and sets flags like CMP.

CPY.description: Computes Y - M and sets flags like CMP.

JMP.description: PC = address. Indirect JMP bug: JMP ($xxFF) reads the high byte from $xx00, not from the next page.

JSR.description: Pushes PC+2 (address of the last byte of JSR) and jumps. With only 128 bytes of RAM, every JSR costs 2 bytes of stack.

LSR.description: Shifts right one bit; bit 0 goes to C, 0 enters bit 7.

PHP.description: Pushes P with B and bit 5 set. On the 2600, 'PHP' with S pointing at a TIA register ($00-$3F mirrors) writes several registers in 3 cycles (e.g. the ENAM0/ENAM1/ENABL trick of Combat).

RTS.description: Pulls PC and adds 1. Pushing an address-1 and doing RTS is a common jump-table trick.

SBC.description: A = A - M - (1 - C). Set C (SEC) before a single-byte subtraction.

SED.description: D = 1: ADC/SBC work in BCD. Handy for scores.

SEI.description: I = 1. Customary at reset even though the 6507 has no IRQ pin.

STA.description: M = A. STA abs,X / abs,Y and (zp),Y always take the extra cycle.

TXS.description: S = X. Pointing S at TIA registers allows PHP/PHA tricks.

LAX.description: A = X = M. Stable except the immediate form (LXA).

DCP.description: M = M - 1, then CMP M. Popular in 2600 kernels: 'DCP counter / BCS' draws a sprite in fewer cycles.

ISB.description: M = M + 1, then SBC M. Also known as ISC.

SLO.description: M = M << 1, then A = A | M.

RLA.description: M = ROL M, then A = A & M.

SRE.description: M = M >> 1, then A = A ^ M.

RRA.description: M = ROR M, then A = A + M + C.

ARR.description: A = ROR(A & #imm) with odd V and C rules.

SBX.description: X = (A & X) - #imm without borrow; flags like CMP. Also known as AXS.

LAS.summary: A = X = S = M AND S (unstable)

LXA.description: Result depends on a 'magic' constant: use LDA #0 first or avoid.

JAM.description: Locks up the processor until reset (also called KIL).
